1 وَغُدَ , aor.
وَغُدَ , (S, K, &c.,) inf. n. وُغَادَةٌ, (L, Msb, K,) He was, or became, a low, or ignoble, mean, or sordid, and weak person, (S, Msb,) who served for the food of his belly: (S, L, Msb:) or light, (L,) stupid, and weak (L, K) in intellect, (L,) low, or ignoble, and mean, or sordid; (L, K;) or weak in body: (L, K:) or light in intellect: or weak as is a slave. (Msb.) ―
-b2- وَغَدَ القَوْمَ, aor. يَغِدُ, (S, L,) inf. n. وَغْدٌ, (L,) He served the people; acted as a servant to them. (S, L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
